title: Message From A: Roommate Edition
trend: TikTok 'Message from A' (an anonymous message signed 'A' calls out an everyday habit while the person is doing it; October 2026 TikTok formats list) with a 'subtle foreshadowing' payoff. Roommates Jordan and Camille keep getting messages from A exposing their habits, suspect their ghost roommate, and learn A is the dog, typing with his nose to get his walk
length_reason: Message from A is a quick one-clip call-out format whose originals run under thirty seconds, so it stays at the low end (3:00), which also keeps it inside Instagram's Reels limit.
youtube_title: Message From A: someone in our apartment sees EVERYTHING (it's not who you think) 📱
description:
Jordan eats cereal over the sink, Camille hides the ketchup, and the ghost roommate steals one sock per load. Then the messages from A start. Watch Archie closely.

#messagefroma #roommates #roommateproblems #comedy #animation #funny #dogsoftiktok
tiktok_caption: message from A 📱 roommate edition (watch the dog) #messagefroma #roommates #comedy #fyp

lines.text: Midnight snack. Nobody is awake. Nobody will ever know.
Message from A. Nice cereal over the sink. Bowls exist, Jordan. A.
Good morning. Why are you eating cereal in the dark like a raccoon?
Someone is watching me. Someone with one letter.
Why is Archie staring at me like that?
He's a dog. That's his whole face.
Message from A. Fourteen alarms is not a morning routine. It is a group project for the whole building. A.
True. I hear every alarm through the wall.
They're all different songs. It's a playlist.
It's a playlist of me crying.
Message from A. Also, those are Camille's slippers. A.
Those are my slippers!
They were by the door. That's basically a donation.
Wait. My phone. Message from A.
Camille. We know you hide the ketchup behind the kale so nobody finds it. A.
You hide my ketchup?
I organize the fridge by color. Ketchup doesn't match anything.
It matches fries, Camille!
Okay. Who in this apartment sees everything and never sleeps?
Bernard.
I beg your pardon. I was in the laundry room, minding my own haunting.
I am a ghost. The walls are my hallway.
Where were you at midnight?
Taking one sock from every load. Like I have since nineteen fifty two.
That's where my socks go?
Oh. Oh dear. A message. Message from A.
Bernard. Use the door. You leave cold spots on the couch. A.
And frankly, I would never sign it A. I would sign it boo.
Phones off. If we can't read it, it can't hurt us.
Archie, stop staring at the phone. It is not a sandwich.
Why is the screen on my phone all wet and smudgy?
Because you eat cereal over the sink, Jordan.
It just turned back on by itself. Message from A.
You said five minutes in March. It is October. A. Sent from a nose.
Sent from a what?
Who did we say five minutes to in March?
The gym. You said that to the gym every day.
It was me. I am A. Archie.
Archie! You can talk?
Nobody listens to the dog. Everybody listens to a mystery.
Why didn't you just say something?
I said walk every morning for three years. You said, aww, who's a good boy.
So I type with my nose. Forty minutes a message. I am exhausted.
That's why the phone is always wet.
And the ketchup?
Ketchup was for Jordan. I am not a monster. I just want my walk.
Okay. Walk at seven. Every day. No five minutes.
And I will stop hiding the ketchup. Mostly.
And the treat jar is not empty. I can hear it. Stop shaking it and saying all gone.
Wait. My phone again. Message from B.
Bernard?
I did tell you. I sign everything boo.
It says, I lived here first, and I would also like a walk. B.
Seven sounds lovely. I will bring the socks.
